detail.longDescription: I'm trying to avoid duplicate requests when two parts of a page need the same data. The part I can't get right is cancellation. If one caller stops waiting, it shouldn't cancel the request for the other caller. Here's a small example. I used a timer so it runs without an API. The result represents already-parsed data, rather than a Response object: const inFlight = new Map(); let started = 0; function fakeLoad(key, signal) { return new Promise((resolve, reject) => { signal.throwIfAborted(); started++; const timer = setTimeout(() => { signal.removeEventListener("abort", onAbort); resolve({ key }); }, 50); function onAbort() { clearTimeout(timer); reject(signal.reason); } signal.addEventListener("abort", onAbort, { once: true }); }); } function loadShared(key, signal) { if (!inFlight.has(key)) { const promise = fakeLoad(key, signal) .finally(() => inFlight.delete(key)); inFlight.set(key, promise); } return inFlight.get(key); } const a = new AbortController(); const b = new AbortController(); const outcomes = Promise.allSettled([ loadShared("settings", a.signal), loadShared("settings", b.signal), ]); a.abort(); outcomes.then(results => { console.log(results.map(result => result.status)); console.log("Underlying loads:", started); }); Aborting a rejects both promises, with one underlying load started. I want A's promise to reject and B's to fulfil, still with only one load started. If I change a.abort() to b.abort() , both fulfil because the second caller's signal is never used. How do I let each caller cancel independently while still sharing the request? The request should only be aborted when nobody is waiting for it anymore. Once that happens, a later caller should be able to start a fresh request.
